# **Data Cleaning**

```{r}
# Showing which columns have null values and how many
music_data %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), ~ sum(is.na(.)))) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "column", values_to = "na_count") %>%
  filter(na_count > 0) %>%
  arrange(desc(na_count))

```

```{r}
# Summary to spot outliers
summary(music_data$Age)

# Count unrealistic ages
sum(music_data$Age < 10 | music_data$Age > 90, na.rm = TRUE)

# View rows with unrealistic ages
music_data %>% 
  filter(Age < 10 | Age > 90)
```

```{r}

# Checking that music hours per day doesn't contain unrealistic # of hours
summary(music_data$Hours.per.day)

music_data %>% 
  filter(Hours.per.day < 0 | Hours.per.day > 16)

# we will remove the 89 year old who listens to rap exclusively while working and has no perceived mental health issues

```

```{r}
cols <- c("Anxiety", "Depression", "Insomnia", "OCD")

# Checking if any values for self reported mental illness are out of the 0-10 range
music_data %>% 
  summarise(across(all_of(cols), 
                   ~ sum(. < 0 | . > 10, na.rm = TRUE)))


```

```{r}
yn_cols <- c(
  "While.working",
  "Instrumentalist",
  "Composer",
  "Exploratory",
  "Foreign.languages"
)

# Checking to see if any of the "yes" "no" columns have values outside of these options
sapply(music_data[yn_cols], function(x) all(x %in% c("Yes", "No")))

lapply(music_data[yn_cols], function(x) setdiff(unique(x), c("Yes", "No")))

sapply(music_data[yn_cols], function(x) sum(x == "", na.rm = TRUE))

# We will drop the rows that having missing values here, as there is no clear way how to impute them


```

```{r}
freq_cols <- c(
  "Frequency..Classical.",
  "Frequency..Country.",
  "Frequency..EDM.",
  "Frequency..Folk.",
  "Frequency..Gospel.",
  "Frequency..Hip.hop.",
  "Frequency..Jazz.",
  "Frequency..K.pop.",
  "Frequency..Latin.",
  "Frequency..Lofi.",
  "Frequency..Metal.",
  "Frequency..Pop.",
  "Frequency..R.B.",
  "Frequency..Rap.",
  "Frequency..Rock.",
  "Frequency..Video.game.music."
)

allowed_freq <- c("Never", "Rarely", "Sometimes", "Very frequently")


# Checking to see if any of the frequency columns have values outside of "Never, Rarely, Sometimes, Very frequently"
sapply(music_data[freq_cols], function(x) sum(!(x %in% allowed_freq)))
```

# **General Data Cleaning**

```{r}
# Cleaning our data

# dropping BPM column
music_data <- music_data %>% select(-any_of("BPM"))

# dropping 1 row that has a null value for Age
music_data <- music_data %>% 
  filter(!is.na(Age))

# Dropping the 89 year old year old who listens to only rap while working 24 hours a day(unrealistic value)
music_data <- music_data %>%
  filter(!(Age == 89 & Hours.per.day == 24))

# Dropping the rows that have non "yes" "no" answers for questions that only permit those values (9 rows were removed here)
allowed_yn <- c("Yes", "No")

music_data <- music_data %>%
  filter(
    if_all(all_of(yn_cols), ~ .x %in% allowed_yn)
  )

# removing 7 rows where Music.effects has an empty string as a response
music_data <- music_data %>%
  filter(Music.effects != "")

# Keep only columns that exist in the data
freq_cols_present <- freq_cols[freq_cols %in% colnames(music_data)]

# Only rename if any of these columns exist
if (length(freq_cols_present) > 0) {
  music_data <- music_data %>%
    rename_with(.cols = all_of(freq_cols_present), 
                .fn = ~ gsub("Frequency\\.\\.", "freq_", .x) %>% 
                       gsub("\\.", "", .))  # Remove all remaining periods
}

music_data_clean <- music_data

glimpse(music_data_clean)

```

# **Research Question 1**

```{r}
# Question 1: How does the number of hours spent listening to music per day vary by depression status and primary streaming service?

# this will be the dataset used for our first research question
music_data_1 <- music_data_clean

unique(music_data_1$Primary.streaming.service)

music_data_1 %>%
  count(Primary.streaming.service)

# removing the row where Primary.streaming.service is empty
music_data_1 <- music_data_1 %>%
  filter(Primary.streaming.service != "")

music_data_1 %>%
  filter(Primary.streaming.service == "I do not use a streaming service.")

# removing the rows where participants stated they do not use a streaming service
music_data_1 <- music_data_1 %>%
  filter(Primary.streaming.service != "I do not use a streaming service.")

music_data_1 %>%
  count(Primary.streaming.service)
```

# **Modeling for Research Question 1**

```{r}
# Question 1: How does the number of hours spent listening to music per day vary by depression status and primary streaming service?

# fit our linear regression model
model_rq1 <- lm(
  Hours.per.day ~ Depression * Primary.streaming.service +
    Age +
    While.working +
    Instrumentalist +
    Composer +
    Exploratory +
    Foreign.languages +
    Anxiety +
    Insomnia +
    OCD +
    Fav.genre +
    Music.effects +
    freq_Classical +
    freq_Country +
    freq_EDM +
    freq_Folk +
    freq_Gospel +
    freq_Hiphop +
    freq_Jazz +
    freq_Kpop +
    freq_Latin +
    freq_Lofi +
    freq_Metal +
    freq_Pop +
    freq_RB +
    freq_Rap +
    freq_Rock +
    freq_Videogamemusic,
  data = music_data_1
)

summary(model_rq1)

```

# **Research Question 2**

```{r}
# Question 2: “How does the number of hours spent listening to music each day impact the severity of reported depression symptoms?”

# Use cleaned dataset
music_data_2 <- music_data_clean

# Fit logistic regression including all relevant predictors
model2 <- glm(
  Depression ~ Hours.per.day +
    Age +
    While.working +
    Instrumentalist +
    Composer +
    Exploratory +
    Foreign.languages +
    Anxiety +
    Insomnia +
    OCD +
    Fav.genre +
    Music.effects +
    freq_Classical +
    freq_Country +
    freq_EDM +
    freq_Folk +
    freq_Gospel +
    freq_Hiphop +
    freq_Jazz +
    freq_Kpop +
    freq_Latin +
    freq_Lofi +
    freq_Metal +
    freq_Pop +
    freq_RB +
    freq_Rap +
    freq_Rock +
    freq_Videogamemusic,
  data = music_data_2,
  family = binomial
)

# View model summary
summary(model2)

# Coefficients on the odds scale
exp(coef(model2))




```
